analysis:
Reviewed all four supplied analyses and available replayed source. The workflow patch at .github/workflows/release-provider.yml head:239–242 explicitly selects production compilation defaults for qualify-sdk; build-provider retains the resolved release environment at head:183. docs/operations/provider-release.md head:315–318 and changelog.d/qualify-sdk-prod-identity.md head:3 describe that test-local distinction. These changes do not themselves grant serving authorization, change signing identity, or bypass durable build approval (A-011, A-017, TB-011, T-052, T-054). No supplied executable change affects prompt encryption, endpoint custody, cache isolation, billing, fan authority or add-on admission.
The analyses also report a synthetic GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT=1 test fixture change at .github/scripts/test-threat-budget.py:930 and unchanged signing/publication controls. Those source excerpts are omitted from this replay, so these claims cannot be independently verified here and are not treated as proof of safety. No independently supported regression warrants a finding.
One material integration contract remains unresolved: qualify-sdk reportedly passes the resolved environment to .github/actions/provider-release-build while now setting prod at job scope. Review that action and provider-swift/Package.swift to establish precedence, build/cache separation, and whether production-default tests preserve the intended qualification contract for a separately dev-configured artifact. The omission establishes neither a bypass nor an unsafe deployment. Replay is incomplete (8 units omitted); this review does not revalidate unchanged provider or platform controls.
